occupation.evidence: References pension, social security, and 'retirement not what we planned'; no mention of current employment.

location.evidence: Found Crohn's throughout colon and terminal ileum.

severity.evidence: Significant damage done by diagnosis, multiple treatment failures, poor quality of life prior to biologic ('quality of life so poor'), and now on Remicade with only partial improvement.

disease_control.evidence: improvement noticeable. Not great but better than before. Can leave house now.

treatments.reason_stopped: Long-term steroids not option at his age with his conditions; bones already weak
treatments.evidence: Added budesonide. Helped temporarily. But long-term steroids not option at my age with my conditions. Bones already weak.
Tried azathioprine. Liver didn't like it. Stopped.
Methotrexate next. The fatigue was unbearable. Already tired from COPD, this made it worse. Couldn't function.
Started Remicade year ago. Infusions tough. Whole day lost. But improvement noticeable. Not great but better than before.

encounters.evidence: Doctor said IBS, common in older men. Gave me fiber.
Changed doctors. New one said diverticulitis. Antibiotics. No improvement.
Finally, third doctor ordered colonoscopy. Found Crohn's throughout colon and terminal ileum.
Doctor wanted biologics from start but I resisted... finally agreed. Started Remicade year ago. Next appointment discussing adding immunomodulator to Remicade.
Neurologist can't determine cause. Might be Crohn's-related, might be medication, might be separate issue.

barriers.evidence: Scared of immune suppression with lung disease. What if get pneumonia? Could be fatal.
Doctor wanted biologics from start but patient resisted due to COPD and fear of fatal pneumonia from immune suppression.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: Three GP/PCP visits before diagnosis, then GI specialist who prescribed biologic = 4 steps total.

extraction_notes: Patient is currently on Remicade (infliximab) with partial response. A future addition of an immunomodulator to Remicade is being discussed at next appointment but not yet started. Peripheral neuropathy onset 6 months ago; cause undetermined. Comorbidities include COPD, peripheral neuropathy, osteoporosis (implied by 'bones already weak'), hypertension (low-sodium diet mentioned), and pre-diabetes. Antibiotics mentioned in the diagnostic phase (for misdiagnosed diverticulitis) were not included in IBD treatments as they were not prescribed for Crohn's. Metformin/diabetes medications, blood pressure medications, and supplements not mentioned and not included.
